action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

557	  include its unsaved edits.
558	- **Filament, another preset:** must be in one of the project's slots
559	  (`not_in_project`), and changes only by being saved (`not_selected` without
560	  `persistAs`). Apply opens it in the filament tab as the sidebar's edit
561	  button does -- `Tab::select_preset`, then `set_filament_idx` for its slot --
562	  then loads and saves through the tab. If the filament open in the tab has
563	  unsaved edits, that switch would discard or prompt, so preview refuses with
564	  `unsaved_edits`.
565	- **Printer, another preset:** a saved printer the project does not use,
566	  saved in place only (`Printers::write_unselected_printer`, the write
567	  `change_named_printer_nozzle` already makes: the difference from its parent,
568	  queued for the cloud). A copy of it would be a second printer made behind
569	  the project's back, so a different `persistAs` is `not_selected`.
570	- The printer allowlist (`writable_printer_setting`) is custom g-code,
571	  printable height, layer-height limits, Z offset, retraction and machine
572	  limits. It excludes the keys that decide which filament and process fit, or
573	  how many extruders there are -- bed shape, nozzle size and type, extruder
574	  count, printer model -- which change with `printer_setup` or
575	  `printer_change`. The filament allowlist (`writable_filament_setting`) is
576	  temperatures, cooling, flow, pressure advance, volumetric speed, density,
577	  cost and custom g-code.
578	- A setting that holds one value per extruder or per nozzle kind keeps its
579	  length: a patch with a different number of values is
580	  `invalid_setting_value`, since a shorter list would drop the rest.
581	
582	`persistAs` is invalid for `object`. It is Orca's Save with the name typed
583	in: the preset's own name overwrites it (`read_only_preset` for one Orca
584	ships, with `"<name> - Copy"`, the name SavePresetDialog offers, as the
585	suggestion); another name that no preset has saves a copy that takes the
586	original's place, in every project slot that used it for a filament
587	(`Sidebar::update_presets_from_to`); a name another preset has is
588	`name_taken`; a name SavePresetDialog would refuse is `invalid_preset_name`.
589	Saving the preset being edited also saves its other unsaved edits, as Save
590	does; preview warns with `saves_unsaved_edits` and lists them. The card's
591	title says where it saves ("; save it", or "; save as \"<name>\""). Without
592	`persistAs`, the tool changes only the edited preset and leaves it dirty.
593	
594	Dialogs the filament and printer tabs would open are refused in preview:
595	a max volumetric speed below 0.5 (`ConfigManipulation::
596	check_filament_max_volumetric_speed`), a first-layer temperature further
597	from the other layers' than `Tab::validate_filament_temperature_pairs`
598	allows when saving, and firmware retraction with a wipe that retracts less
599	than 100% first (`TabPrinter::toggle_options`).
600	
601	### Scope expansion acceptance criteria
602	
603	- The registry exposes the same required `scope` enum and target shape through
604	  the in-app and MCP adapters; catalog tests pin both projections.
605	- Argument tests reject omitted or unknown scopes and every missing, extra,
606	  zero-based, mixed, or malformed target. No test accepts the old call shape.
607	- Search, get, preview, and apply each have fake- and real-adapter coverage for
608	  all four scopes, including a readable but unwritable key.
609	- Filament tests cover a preset in a slot that is not open in its tab, a copy
610	  taking its slot, and a dirty preset that cannot be changed without an
611	  implicit switch or discard.
612	- Printer tests prove that a normal writable value updates the native field,
613	  dirty marker, slice invalidation, and read-back value, while topology and
614	  compatibility keys remain unwritable.
615	- Apply tests prove atomic failure, scope-specific activity text, preset revert
616	  or inverse-patch behavior, and project Undo only for object overrides.
617	- Evals and deterministic-agent fixtures use explicit scopes before the old
618	  schema is removed; there is no dual-schema phase.
619	
620	### Error codes
621	
622	| Condition | Code |
623	|---|---|
624	| missing or unknown `scope`; forbidden, missing, or malformed `target`; `persistAs` for an object | `invalid_arguments` |
625	| no visible preset of that scope has the target's name | `unknown_preset` with suggestions |
626	| a filament or printer preset that is not being edited, without `persistAs`, or a copy of a printer not in use | `not_selected` |
627	| a filament that is in none of the project's slots, changed by name | `not_in_project` |
628	| `persistAs` overwriting a preset Orca ships | `read_only_preset`, suggesting `"<name> - Copy"` |
629	| `persistAs` naming another existing preset | `name_taken` |
630	| `persistAs` SavePresetDialog would refuse | `invalid_preset_name` |
631	| key not in the definition table | `unknown_setting` with suggestions |
632	| known key not applicable to the requested scope | `unsupported_scope` |
633	| readable key outside that scope's allowlist | `unsupported_setting_mutation` |
634	| requested object is gone, or no FFF printer or process is selected | `workspace_unavailable` |
635	| opening a filament in its tab would discard another dirty edited preset | `unsaved_edits` |
636	| parse failure, bound violation, or layer height outside the printer's range | `invalid_setting_value` with `allowed` or bounds |
637	| a scope-specific dependency or validator rule conflicts | `incompatible_settings` with the conflicting keys |
638	| session, revision, target mapping, preset, or before value changed since preview | `stale_workspace` with expected and current |
639	| client cancelled or the app closed | `cancelled` |
640	| the batch call failed after validation | `execution_failed` |

642	Preview never fails for content reasons. Apply fails with the first blocking
643	code and mutates nothing. Never convert an invariant failure into success.

645	### Orca entry points the tools use
646	
647	- **Process atomic batch:** `Tab::load_config(const DynamicPrintConfig&)` in
648	  `src/slic3r/GUI/Tab.cpp` diffs against the edited preset, sets every changed
649	  key, then runs `update_dirty()`, `reload_config()`, and `update()` once.
650	  `TabPrint::update()` runs the FFF normalizer and reaches
651	  `Plater::on_config_change`, which invalidates slicing as a sidebar edit
652	  would. Apply is therefore: build a config holding only the changed keys and
653	  call `wxGetApp().get_tab(Preset::TYPE_PRINT)->load_config(diff)`.
654	- **Filament and printer batches:** use the same `Tab::load_config` owner on
655	  `Preset::TYPE_FILAMENT` or `Preset::TYPE_PRINTER`, but only after preview
656	  models that tab's dependencies, compatibility consequences and dialog
657	  predicates. A scope is not complete until a real-adapter test proves the
658	  native fields, dirty marker, slicing invalidation and read-back values.
659	- **Parsing:** clone the scoped config and `set_deserialize(key, text)` per
660	  key; Orca throws for unknown keys and unparseable values. Canonical value is
661	  `option->serialize()` after parsing.
662	- **Bounds and enums:** `ConfigOptionDef` in `src/libslic3r/Config.hpp`
663	  (`type`, `label`, `category`, `tooltip`, `sidetext`, `min`, `max`, `mode`,
664	  `readonly`, `enum_values`, `enum_labels`). Treat `min` and `max` as absent
665	  when they are the float limits.
666	- **Validation:** build the full effective configuration with the scoped clone
667	  installed, then run the validator appropriate to that owner. Process and
668	  object continue to use `Slic3r::validate(const FullPrintConfig&)`. Do not
669	  assume that process normalization covers filament or printer dependencies.
670	- **Dirty state:** use the owning `PresetCollection`'s dirty and
671	  different-from-parent APIs. The result must name the owning preset and
672	  whether it is dirty after the call.

674	### The process normalizer can open dialogs and rewrite values
675	
676	`update_print_fff_config` and `toggle_print_fff_options` in
677	`src/slic3r/GUI/ConfigManipulation.cpp` run inside `TabPrint::update()` after
678	every batch and evaluate every rule against the whole post-batch config, not
679	only the changed keys. Some rules open a modal dialog and then rewrite a
680	value; others rewrite silently. A modal opened from inside a tool execution
681	blocks the GUI thread while the request waits, and a silent rewrite makes the
682	result lie unless it is reported.
683	
684	Two rules follow. Preview evaluates the same rule set against a clone, using
685	the printer preset and filament count the adapter can read, so a rule that
686	fires because of a pre-existing value is reported too. Dialog rules are
687	blocking issues; silent rules are warnings that name the dependent key and
688	its predicted value (`normalized_dependency`), and apply lists the actual
689	rewrite under `normalized`. Preview reuses Orca's `ConfigManipulation` on the
690	clone with no presentation callbacks rather than copying its option tables.
691	
692	Rules reachable through the current allowlist, as audited when the tools
693	were built. Line numbers drift; search for the condition text.
694	
695	| Rule in Orca | Reached by | Effect | Preview must |
696	|---|---|---|---|
697	| `layer_height` at or below epsilon | `layer_height` | modal, reset to 0.2 | refuse with `invalid_setting_value` and the minimum |
698	| `layer_height` above the printer's `max_layer_height` when that exceeds 0.2 | `layer_height` | modal, clamp | refuse with `invalid_setting_value` and the printer's maximum |
699	| `seam_slope_type` not `None` and absolute `seam_slope_start_height` at or above `layer_height` | lowering `layer_height` | modal, start height reset to 0 | refuse with `incompatible_settings`; evaluate percent values through `get_abs_value`, 100% or above also trips it |
700	| `spiral_mode` on and not all of `wall_loops` 1, `top_shell_layers` 0, `sparse_infill_density` 0 | those three keys | yes/no dialog, several keys rewritten either way | refuse with `incompatible_settings` naming `spiral_mode` |
701	| `sparse_infill_pattern` without multiline support while `fill_multiline` is above 1 | `sparse_infill_pattern` | silent: `fill_multiline` reset to 1 | predict and report as `normalized_dependency` |
702	| support-gap rounding block | none; it is inside `#if 0` | inactive | do not predict a change that does not happen |
703	| `support_style` not in the set for the support type (normal: default, grid, snug; tree: default, tree_slim, tree_strong, tree_hybrid, organic) | `enable_support`, `support_type`, `support_style` | silent: style reset to default | refuse with `invalid_setting_value` and the fitting styles in `allowed`; the patch is fixed by the caller, not rewritten |
704	| global `enable_support` while `detect_overhang_wall` is off | `enable_support` | silent: `detect_overhang_wall` turned on, once per query state | predict and report as `normalized_dependency` |
705	| `spiral_mode` on with support or thin walls | `enable_support`, `detect_thin_wall` | yes/no dialog | refuse with `incompatible_settings` (the spiral row above) |
706	| fuzzy skin in an Extrusion or Combined mode without Arachne | `wall_generator` set to classic | yes/no dialog | refuse with `incompatible_settings` naming `fuzzy_skin_mode` |
707	| `Tab::on_value_change` for `support_type` in simple mode (style reset) and for the support filaments (dialogs) | none: `Tab::load_config` never calls `on_value_change`, and the filament keys are not writable | inactive for tools | nothing |
708	| `toggle_print_fff_options` writes (`enable_arc_fitting`, the slope segment length, `fill_multiline`, `overhang_reverse_threshold`) | none of the new keys directly; the prediction runs the real pass on the clone | silent | report whatever the clone shows |

716	walls, overhang reversal, timelapse, and wrapping detection. The real-adapter

718	allowlisted key under every row above (the support, brim and style checks apply a tree-support patch with the support page shown and read the native fields back), and that every predicted silent
719	rewrite appears in the result with its actual value. A rule found later that
720	a tool can trigger is a defect in the preview, not accepted behavior. Adding
721	a key to the allowlist means re-reading both functions for every place that
722	key is read and extending this table.

724	### Apply binds the previewed values
725	
726	Apply is previewed three times. The client previews and sees before and
727	after values. When queuing the action the coordinator previews again on the GUI
728	thread, so an invalid patch fails at once, and stores that result as the
729	previewed set. The activity title names the keys from it. At execution the adapter previews a third time
730	against the then-current config and compares every before value against the
731	confirmed set: a moved value is `stale_workspace`, a blocking issue is
732	`invalid_settings`, and neither mutates. Client-supplied values are never
733	trusted as before values. Where Orca normalized a value differently from the
734	preview, the actual value is returned and the key is listed under
735	`normalized`; the mutation happened, so that is a success with an honest
736	report.
737	
738	### Per-object overrides
739	
740	`scope: "object"` with `target: {"objectId": "..."}` reads the value the
741	object prints with: its own override where `ModelConfig` has one
742	(`overridden: true`), otherwise the process value.
743	A patch is checked against the process config with the object's overrides and
744	the patch applied, with the same parsing, bounds, dialog predicates, support
745	style rule, and `Slic3r::validate` as a process patch. Keys that are neither
746	`PrintRegionConfig` nor `PrintObjectConfig` options (ObjectList's own list
747	for a whole object) are refused with `unsupported_scope`. No dependencies are
748	predicted: Orca runs the normalizer only on the process preset and on edits
749	made in the object settings panel, so an override is stored as written.
750	
751	Apply takes one `Plater::TakeSnapshot` ("Change object settings"), writes each
752	key with `ModelConfig::set_key_value`, calls
753	`ObjectList::object_config_options_changed` so the list shows the settings
754	item, and `Plater::changed_object` so that object's slicing is invalidated.
755	The result says `projectUndo: true`; project Undo removes the override. The activity names the object. The coordinator looks the object up in the
756	current snapshot when queued and at execution and fails with `missing_object`
757	when it is gone; the adapter treats a missing target as a broken precondition.
758	No patch value removes an override; Undo, or the object settings panel,
759	does.

761	### Registry facts worth knowing
762	
763	- `ToolExecutionCoordinator::execute` dispatches on `ToolHandler` with
764	  explicit blocks; add a block per tool, not a generic dispatch table.
765	- `kInvalidatingReasons` is the mask for most queued actions and includes
766	  `Settings`, so a queued action fails with `stale_revision` when the user
767	  edits a setting in the GUI. `settings_apply_patch` has its own mask,
768	  `Settings | Project`: the M5 live eval showed an agent annotating a region
769	  between its settings preview and its apply, and the model edit (and the
770	  slicing events after it) made every apply stale. A settings patch is bound
771	  to the before values it previewed, which the apply checks again, so its
772	  `expectedRevision` only has to be no older than the last settings or project
773	  change; model edits do not matter.
774	- `ToolRegistry::validate_output` accepts a closed schema vocabulary: `type`,
775	  `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties`, `items`, `minimum`,
776	  `maxItems`, `enum`, `maxLength`. Any other keyword throws; extend the
777	  validator with a test before using a new keyword. `enum` is checked whatever
778	  the value's type; `maxLength` counts UTF-8 bytes, matching the byte bounds
779	  this registry states everywhere else.

792	## Proportional security growth
793	
794	The server starts automatically, binds numeric loopback, validates browser origins, and enforces request limits. It has no bearer authentication or per-call confirmation. Any local process that can reach the socket can execute exposed tools, including mutations and validated file operations. Origin validation protects the browser boundary; it does not identify local processes. Never expose this endpoint beyond loopback.
795	
796	Revisit the security design before adding remote access, cross-restart grants, multiple permission levels, camera data, printer upload, or physical print start. At that point evaluate authenticated pairing, durable credential storage, per-client scopes, revocation, rate controls, privacy review, and a dedicated audit log.
797	
798	Caller-supplied paths remain narrowly constrained. `project_open` and `object_import_file` accept absolute readable paths; `export_file` requires the expected extension, an existing parent directory, an explicit `overwrite` flag for replacement, and refuses OrcaSlicer's data and temporary project directories. `project_attachment_read` resolves only an attachment ID inside the project attachment directory. These constraints reduce accidental scope; they are not a substitute for authenticating local clients.

864	## Definition of done
865	
866	A new tool is done when:
867	
868	- it fixes a named eval failure;
869	- its scope and authority are honest;
870	- the registry is the only definition source;
871	- the coordinator owns policy and lifecycle;
872	- the real operation uses Orca's current owner on the GUI thread;
873	- results and errors are structured and bounded;
874	- mutation history, staleness, events, and cancellation behave as documented;
875	- fake, real-adapter, adapter, protocol, and shell evidence pass as applicable;
876	- no unrelated Orca behavior changes when the JusPrin feature is disabled; and
877	- the PR records any upstream seam and its rebase evidence.
878	
879	Tool count is not the success metric. A compact catalog that reliably completes real printing tasks is.

include its unsaved edits.
- **Filament, another preset:** must be in one of the project's slots
  (`not_in_project`), and changes only by being saved (`not_selected` without
  `persistAs`). Apply opens it in the filament tab as the sidebar's edit
  button does -- `Tab::select_preset`, then `set_filament_idx` for its slot --
  then loads and saves through the tab. If the filament open in the tab has
  unsaved edits, that switch would discard or prompt, so preview refuses with
  `unsaved_edits`.
- **Printer, another preset:** a saved printer the project does not use,
  saved in place only (`Printers::write_unselected_printer`, the write
  `change_named_printer_nozzle` already makes: the difference from its parent,
  queued for the cloud). A copy of it would be a second printer made behind
  the project's back, so a different `persistAs` is `not_selected`.
- The printer allowlist (`writable_printer_setting`) is custom g-code,
  printable height, layer-height limits, Z offset, retraction and machine
  limits. It excludes the keys that decide which filament and process fit, or
  how many extruders there are -- bed shape, nozzle size and type, extruder
  count, printer model -- which change with `printer_setup` or
  `printer_change`. The filament allowlist (`writable_filament_setting`) is
  temperatures, cooling, flow, pressure advance, volumetric speed, density,
  cost and custom g-code.
- A setting that holds one value per extruder or per nozzle kind keeps its
  length: a patch with a different number of values is
  `invalid_setting_value`, since a shorter list would drop the rest.

`persistAs` is invalid for `object`. It is Orca's Save with the name typed
in: the preset's own name overwrites it (`read_only_preset` for one Orca
ships, with `"<name> - Copy"`, the name SavePresetDialog offers, as the
suggestion); another name that no preset has saves a copy that takes the
original's place, in every project slot that used it for a filament
(`Sidebar::update_presets_from_to`); a name another preset has is
`name_taken`; a name SavePresetDialog would refuse is `invalid_preset_name`.
Saving the preset being edited also saves its other unsaved edits, as Save
does; preview warns with `saves_unsaved_edits` and lists them. The card's
title says where it saves ("; save it", or "; save as \"<name>\""). Without
`persistAs`, the tool changes only the edited preset and leaves it dirty.

Dialogs the filament and printer tabs would open are refused in preview:
a max volumetric speed below 0.5 (`ConfigManipulation::
check_filament_max_volumetric_speed`), a first-layer temperature further
from the other layers' than `Tab::validate_filament_temperature_pairs`
allows when saving, and firmware retraction with a wipe that retracts less
than 100% first (`TabPrinter::toggle_options`).

### Scope expansion acceptance criteria

- The registry exposes the same required `scope` enum and target shape through
  the in-app and MCP adapters; catalog tests pin both projections.
- Argument tests reject omitted or unknown scopes and every missing, extra,
  zero-based, mixed, or malformed target. No test accepts the old call shape.
- Search, get, preview, and apply each have fake- and real-adapter coverage for
  all four scopes, including a readable but unwritable key.
- Filament tests cover a preset in a slot that is not open in its tab, a copy
  taking its slot, and a dirty preset that cannot be changed without an
  implicit switch or discard.
- Printer tests prove that a normal writable value updates the native field,
  dirty marker, slice invalidation, and read-back value, while topology and
  compatibility keys remain unwritable.
- Apply tests prove atomic failure, scope-specific activity text, preset revert
  or inverse-patch behavior, and project Undo only for object overrides.
- Evals and deterministic-agent fixtures use explicit scopes before the old
  schema is removed; there is no dual-schema phase.

### Error codes

| Condition | Code |
|---|---|
| missing or unknown `scope`; forbidden, missing, or malformed `target`; `persistAs` for an object | `invalid_arguments` |
| no visible preset of that scope has the target's name | `unknown_preset` with suggestions |
| a filament or printer preset that is not being edited, without `persistAs`, or a copy of a printer not in use | `not_selected` |
| a filament that is in none of the project's slots, changed by name | `not_in_project` |
| `persistAs` overwriting a preset Orca ships | `read_only_preset`, suggesting `"<name> - Copy"` |
| `persistAs` naming another existing preset | `name_taken` |
| `persistAs` SavePresetDialog would refuse | `invalid_preset_name` |
| key not in the definition table | `unknown_setting` with suggestions |
| known key not applicable to the requested scope | `unsupported_scope` |
| readable key outside that scope's allowlist | `unsupported_setting_mutation` |
| requested object is gone, or no FFF printer or process is selected | `workspace_unavailable` |
| opening a filament in its tab would discard another dirty edited preset | `unsaved_edits` |
| parse failure, bound violation, or layer height outside the printer's range | `invalid_setting_value` with `allowed` or bounds |
| a scope-specific dependency or validator rule conflicts | `incompatible_settings` with the conflicting keys |
| session, revision, target mapping, preset, or before value changed since preview | `stale_workspace` with expected and current |
| client cancelled or the app closed | `cancelled` |
| the batch call failed after validation | `execution_failed` |

Preview never fails for content reasons. Apply fails with the first blocking
code and mutates nothing. Never convert an invariant failure into success.

### Orca entry points the tools use

- **Process atomic batch:** `Tab::load_config(const DynamicPrintConfig&)` in
  `src/slic3r/GUI/Tab.cpp` diffs against the edited preset, sets every changed
  key, then runs `update_dirty()`, `reload_config()`, and `update()` once.
  `TabPrint::update()` runs the FFF normalizer and reaches
  `Plater::on_config_change`, which invalidates slicing as a sidebar edit
  would. Apply is therefore: build a config holding only the changed keys and
  call `wxGetApp().get_tab(Preset::TYPE_PRINT)->load_config(diff)`.
- **Filament and printer batches:** use the same `Tab::load_config` owner on
  `Preset::TYPE_FILAMENT` or `Preset::TYPE_PRINTER`, but only after preview
  models that tab's dependencies, compatibility consequences and dialog
  predicates. A scope is not complete until a real-adapter test proves the
  native fields, dirty marker, slicing invalidation and read-back values.
- **Parsing:** clone the scoped config and `set_deserialize(key, text)` per
  key; Orca throws for unknown keys and unparseable values. Canonical value is
  `option->serialize()` after parsing.
- **Bounds and enums:** `ConfigOptionDef` in `src/libslic3r/Config.hpp`
  (`type`, `label`, `category`, `tooltip`, `sidetext`, `min`, `max`, `mode`,
  `readonly`, `enum_values`, `enum_labels`). Treat `min` and `max` as absent
  when they are the float limits.
- **Validation:** build the full effective configuration with the scoped clone
  installed, then run the validator appropriate to that owner. Process and
  object continue to use `Slic3r::validate(const FullPrintConfig&)`. Do not
  assume that process normalization covers filament or printer dependencies.
- **Dirty state:** use the owning `PresetCollection`'s dirty and
  different-from-parent APIs. The result must name the owning preset and
  whether it is dirty after the call.

### The process normalizer can open dialogs and rewrite values

`update_print_fff_config` and `toggle_print_fff_options` in
`src/slic3r/GUI/ConfigManipulation.cpp` run inside `TabPrint::update()` after
every batch and evaluate every rule against the whole post-batch config, not
only the changed keys. Some rules open a modal dialog and then rewrite a
value; others rewrite silently. A modal opened from inside a tool execution
blocks the GUI thread while the request waits, and a silent rewrite makes the
result lie unless it is reported.

Two rules follow. Preview evaluates the same rule set against a clone, using
the printer preset and filament count the adapter can read, so a rule that
fires because of a pre-existing value is reported too. Dialog rules are
blocking issues; silent rules are warnings that name the dependent key and
its predicted value (`normalized_dependency`), and apply lists the actual
rewrite under `normalized`. Preview reuses Orca's `ConfigManipulation` on the
clone with no presentation callbacks rather than copying its option tables.

Rules reachable through the current allowlist, as audited when the tools
were built. Line numbers drift; search for the condition text.

| Rule in Orca | Reached by | Effect | Preview must |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layer_height` at or below epsilon | `layer_height` | modal, reset to 0.2 | refuse with `invalid_setting_value` and the minimum |
| `layer_height` above the printer's `max_layer_height` when that exceeds 0.2 | `layer_height` | modal, clamp | refuse with `invalid_setting_value` and the printer's maximum |
| `seam_slope_type` not `None` and absolute `seam_slope_start_height` at or above `layer_height` | lowering `layer_height` | modal, start height reset to 0 | refuse with `incompatible_settings`; evaluate percent values through `get_abs_value`, 100% or above also trips it |
| `spiral_mode` on and not all of `wall_loops` 1, `top_shell_layers` 0, `sparse_infill_density` 0 | those three keys | yes/no dialog, several keys rewritten either way | refuse with `incompatible_settings` naming `spiral_mode` |
| `sparse_infill_pattern` without multiline support while `fill_multiline` is above 1 | `sparse_infill_pattern` | silent: `fill_multiline` reset to 1 | predict and report as `normalized_dependency` |
| support-gap rounding block | none; it is inside `#if 0` | inactive | do not predict a change that does not happen |
| `support_style` not in the set for the support type (normal: default, grid, snug; tree: default, tree_slim, tree_strong, tree_hybrid, organic) | `enable_support`, `support_type`, `support_style` | silent: style reset to default | refuse with `invalid_setting_value` and the fitting styles in `allowed`; the patch is fixed by the caller, not rewritten |
| global `enable_support` while `detect_overhang_wall` is off | `enable_support` | silent: `detect_overhang_wall` turned on, once per query state | predict and report as `normalized_dependency` |
| `spiral_mode` on with support or thin walls | `enable_support`, `detect_thin_wall` | yes/no dialog | refuse with `incompatible_settings` (the spiral row above) |
| fuzzy skin in an Extrusion or Combined mode without Arachne | `wall_generator` set to classic | yes/no dialog | refuse with `incompatible_settings` naming `fuzzy_skin_mode` |
| `Tab::on_value_change` for `support_type` in simple mode (style reset) and for the support filaments (dialogs) | none: `Tab::load_config` never calls `on_value_change`, and the filament keys are not writable | inactive for tools | nothing |
| `toggle_print_fff_options` writes (`enable_arc_fitting`, the slope segment length, `fill_multiline`, `overhang_reverse_threshold`) | none of the new keys directly; the prediction runs the real pass on the clone | silent | report whatever the clone shows |

The brim, skirt, seam, speed, surface-pattern, interface, contact-distance, threshold and shell-thickness keys are read by no rule in either function beyond enabling or disabling their own fields; the audit covered both functions and `Tab.cpp`'s `on_value_change` on 2026-09-16. Open-enum keys (the interface layer counts) carry no `allowed` list: their enum values are shortcuts, and any number in bounds is accepted. A boolean has no numeric bounds.

Every active dialog predicate must be checked, including pre-existing
invalid ironing spacing, first-layer height, XY and elephant-foot
compensation, alternate-extra-wall, infill-lock depth, and fuzzy-skin
settings; spiral mode also checks support, enforced support layers, thin
walls, overhang reversal, timelapse, and wrapping detection. The real-adapter
test asserts that no top-level dialog appears during apply for any
allowlisted key under every row above (the support, brim and style checks apply a tree-support patch with the support page shown and read the native fields back), and that every predicted silent
rewrite appears in the result with its actual value. A rule found later that
a tool can trigger is a defect in the preview, not accepted behavior. Adding
a key to the allowlist means re-reading both functions for every place that
key is read and extending this table.

### Apply binds the previewed values

Apply is previewed three times. The client previews and sees before and
after values. When queuing the action the coordinator previews again on the GUI
thread, so an invalid patch fails at once, and stores that result as the
previewed set. The activity title names the keys from it. At execution the adapter previews a third time
against the then-current config and compares every before value against the
confirmed set: a moved value is `stale_workspace`, a blocking issue is
`invalid_settings`, and neither mutates. Client-supplied values are never
trusted as before values. Where Orca normalized a value differently from the
preview, the actual value is returned and the key is listed under
`normalized`; the mutation happened, so that is a success with an honest
report.

### Per-object overrides

`scope: "object"` with `target: {"objectId": "..."}` reads the value the
object prints with: its own override where `ModelConfig` has one
(`overridden: true`), otherwise the process value.
A patch is checked against the process config with the object's overrides and
the patch applied, with the same parsing, bounds, dialog predicates, support
style rule, and `Slic3r::validate` as a process patch. Keys that are neither
`PrintRegionConfig` nor `PrintObjectConfig` options (ObjectList's own list
for a whole object) are refused with `unsupported_scope`. No dependencies are
predicted: Orca runs the normalizer only on the process preset and on edits
made in the object settings panel, so an override is stored as written.

Apply takes one `Plater::TakeSnapshot` ("Change object settings"), writes each
key with `ModelConfig::set_key_value`, calls
`ObjectList::object_config_options_changed` so the list shows the settings
item, and `Plater::changed_object` so that object's slicing is invalidated.
The result says `projectUndo: true`; project Undo removes the override. The activity names the object. The coordinator looks the object up in the
current snapshot when queued and at execution and fails with `missing_object`
when it is gone; the adapter treats a missing target as a broken precondition.
No patch value removes an override; Undo, or the object settings panel,
does.

### Registry facts worth knowing

- `ToolExecutionCoordinator::execute` dispatches on `ToolHandler` with
  explicit blocks; add a block per tool, not a generic dispatch table.
- `kInvalidatingReasons` is the mask for most queued actions and includes
  `Settings`, so a queued action fails with `stale_revision` when the user
  edits a setting in the GUI. `settings_apply_patch` has its own mask,
  `Settings | Project`: the M5 live eval showed an agent annotating a region
  between its settings preview and its apply, and the model edit (and the
  slicing events after it) made every apply stale. A settings patch is bound
  to the before values it previewed, which the apply checks again, so its
  `expectedRevision` only has to be no older than the last settings or project
  change; model edits do not matter.
- `ToolRegistry::validate_output` accepts a closed schema vocabulary: `type`,
  `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties`, `items`, `minimum`,
  `maxItems`, `enum`, `maxLength`. Any other keyword throws; extend the
  validator with a test before using a new keyword. `enum` is checked whatever
  the value's type; `maxLength` counts UTF-8 bytes, matching the byte bounds
  this registry states everywhere else.

### Upstream seams the tool system owns

Two added lines in `src/CMakeLists.txt`, eight in
`src/dev-utils/platform/unix/build_linux_image.sh.in`, and one additive
`notify_project_state_changed(ProjectStateChangeReason::Settings)` call at
the end of `Plater::on_config_change`. `GUI_Utils.hpp` gains one declaration and two lines at the top of `DPIAware::ShowModal` (`answer_modal`, defined in fork code); if upstream changes that function, keep both. `Plater::priv::load_files` gains a first-line `FileLoadScope` and a call after `load_config_model` to mark settings actually applied. The file-open entry points gain `FileOpenScope` to include choices before loading begins. The two model metadata resets at the start of `Plater::load_project` were moved below its cancelable checks so an aborted open leaves the project intact; carry those resets to that later point on rebase. `FileLoads.hpp` is reached through the neutral `ProjectState.hpp` forwarding header. `libslic3r/Orient.hpp` and `.cpp` gain `score_orientations`, additive beside `orient()`; it reuses `AutoOrienter` and duplicates the five lines of `process()` that build Orca's candidate set. Current upstream (72774e5398) reworks `Orient.cpp` for cooling-fan orientation and removes `OrientParamsArea`, which the adapter copies from today's `OrientJob`: the text merges cleanly, but at that rebase `score_orientations` must be rechecked against the new `AutoOrienter` and the adapter must build its parameters the way the new `OrientJob` does. `Plater.cpp` is the fork's busiest
file; when that function changes upstream, the natural resolution is "keep
both". No line in `Tab.cpp`, `ConfigManipulation.cpp`, or `PrintConfig.cpp`
changes; the normalizer hazards are handled by refusing the inputs in
fork-owned code.

## Proportional security growth

The server starts automatically, binds numeric loopback, validates browser origins, and enforces request limits. It has no bearer authentication or per-call confirmation. Any local process that can reach the socket can execute exposed tools, including mutations and validated file operations. Origin validation protects the browser boundary; it does not identify local processes. Never expose this endpoint beyond loopback.

Revisit the security design before adding remote access, cross-restart grants, multiple permission levels, camera data, printer upload, or physical print start. At that point evaluate authenticated pairing, durable credential storage, per-client scopes, revocation, rate controls, privacy review, and a dedicated audit log.

Caller-supplied paths remain narrowly constrained. `project_open` and `object_import_file` accept absolute readable paths; `export_file` requires the expected extension, an existing parent directory, an explicit `overwrite` flag for replacement, and refuses OrcaSlicer's data and temporary project directories. `project_attachment_read` resolves only an attachment ID inside the project attachment directory. These constraints reduce accidental scope; they are not a substitute for authenticating local clients.

On 2026-09-16 it failed on Windows: `select_object(0)` returned false after `load_files`, seven checks failed, and the process died with `0xC0000005`. The test code was not stale. The cause was the machine setup. The Mesa provisioning script put `opengl32.dll` only in `mesa\`, where only the app launcher looks for it. A harness has no launcher, so this one ran on the system's GL 1.1 and its canvas never initialized. Selection is built from the canvas's volumes, so nothing could be selected, and the gizmo check then opened a paint gizmo with nothing selected. The script now also copies `opengl32.dll` beside each harness (see "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in [engineering-method.md](engineering-method.md)); re-run it on existing build trees. With GL in place, two harness faults surfaced that only Windows shows:

- The move-event check asserted that the move was the last change. On Windows, queued `EVT_GLCANVAS_OBJECT_SELECT` events publish two Selection-only changes after it, so the check now skips those.
- The data-directory cleanup threw, because the open log file cannot be deleted, and the uncaught exception turned a PASS into `0xC0000409`. It now warns instead, as the shell harness already did.

Pulling the script change does not fix a build tree that was already provisioned; run the script on it again. So that a tree without GL cannot fail this way unnoticed again, the harness now checks, right after its first model load, that the canvas initialized GL. If it did not, the harness stops with `HARNESS ERROR the 3D canvas did not initialize OpenGL` and the command to fix it, exits 1, and does not crash. A clean exit on that early path also needed the harness to close the main frame, as the shell harness does. It used to call `ExitMainLoop()`, which skips `MainFrame::shutdown()`, and a pending project backup then posted to the deleted frame.

Node is required: the Agent and Home pages are built from TypeScript and their `index.html` is generated, not committed, so a tree without npm fails at configure time and an app built without them shows no Agent panel at all.

The Python bridge tests run there too, with the helper named explicitly, since the default path in `tests/mcp/test_bridge_process.py` is the macOS bundle:

```sh
JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=build/src/Release/jusprin-mcp.exe python -m unittest discover -s tests/mcp

Eight live-peer tests failed on Windows — SSE progress, client cancellation, EOF with a pending call, stdout backpressure, the live catalog's header mirroring, and a malformed peer result — and the same eight failed from commits well before the M0 work, which is why they were first recorded here as an unexamined platform gap. Examining them found a single cause, and it was the helper's, not the tests': Windows hands `main()` its arguments and `getenv()` its values in the active code page, so `fs::u8path(argv[i])` could not spell the fixture's `discovery 打印.json`, `read_discovery` never found the file, every call fell back to the offline catalog, and nothing that needs a live peer could pass. The helper now takes anything that becomes a path from `CommandLineToArgvW` and `GetEnvironmentVariableW`; POSIX argv already carries the native bytes and is unchanged. The standing rule: in helper code a path may never arrive through a narrow Windows API, and the fixture's non-ASCII name earns its keep by catching exactly this.

Nothing else in the stdio contract differs on Windows — non-blocking stdout, SSE framing, cancellation and teardown all behave as the tests assume, including twenty consecutive runs of the blocked-stdout and backpressure cases. The same run also caught `tools/list` still asserting the pre-M0 catalog size, which the milestone updated in the C++ tests and not here. Run this suite on Windows for every milestone; a macOS pass is not evidence for it.

Catalog bytes per tool, the measurement every milestone PR reports, without `python3`. ## Definition of done

A new tool is done when:

- it fixes a named eval failure;
- its scope and authority are honest;
- the registry is the only definition source;
- the coordinator owns policy and lifecycle;
- the real operation uses Orca's current owner on the GUI thread;
- results and errors are structured and bounded;
- mutation history, staleness, events, and cancellation behave as documented;
- fake, real-adapter, adapter, protocol, and shell evidence pass as applicable;
- no unrelated Orca behavior changes when the JusPrin feature is disabled; and
- the PR records any upstream seam and its rebase evidence.

Tool count is not the success metric. A compact catalog that reliably completes real printing tasks is.

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

p='src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp'
s=open(p).read()
old=s[s.index('Reply discovery(const Request& request)'):s.index('Reply list_tools(')]
new='''// What an MCP client's model reads when it connects: the patterns that span
// tools and the server's constraints, for someone else's agent. A tool's own
// description says how that tool works. The in-app assistant's print guidance
// (Agent::kPrintJourneyGuidance) is not sent here: it asks for a setup title,
// which belongs to an in-app chat and is refused from MCP.
constexpr const char* kInstructions =
    "These tools act on the project open in the running JusPrin app, which the user may be editing at the same time. "
    "Read the current state with workspace_inspect before changing it. Where a change has a dry run "
    "(settings_preview_patch, printer_setup_preview, object_divide_preview), preview first; settings_apply_patch takes "
    "the sessionId and revision its preview returned. A stale_workspace error means the project changed after your "
    "read: read and preview again before retrying. For a print request, record the requirements the user stated as "
    "intent_update fields, and your plan with plan_set, before changing the project. Check a slice with slice_report "
    "before writing its G-code with export_file. Closing a response cancels its pending work.";

Reply discovery(const Request& request)
{
    return {200, rpc_result(request.id, {{"supportedVersions", json::array({kProtocolVersion})},
                                         {"capabilities", {{"tools", {{"listChanged", false}}}}},
                                         {"ttlMs", 0},
                                         {"cacheScope", "private"},
                                         {"instructions", kInstructions}})};
}

'''
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.hpp'
s=open(p).read()
old='''// How a print request goes, for both adapters' instructions: the tools'
// own descriptions say how each one works.
'''
new='''// How a print request goes, for the in-app assistant's prompt only: it names
// the setup title an in-app chat owns. MCP clients get their own instructions
// (kInstructions in Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp). The tools' own descriptions say how
// each one works.
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='tests/agent/test_mcp_runtime.cpp'
s=open(p).read()
old='''    // What they do ask for, intent fields, MCP records.
    CHECK(instructions.find("intent_update") != std::string::npos);
'''
new='''    // What they do ask for, intent fields, MCP records.
    CHECK(instructions.find("intent_update") != std::string::npos);
    FakeProductState store;
    h.coordinator.set_product_state(&store);
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
s=s.replace('#include "../jusprin_support/FakeWorkspace.hpp"\n','#include "../jusprin_support/FakeProductState.hpp"\n#include "../jusprin_support/FakeWorkspace.hpp"\n',1)
open(p,'w').write(s)

MCP clients now get their own short instructions that only describe calls the MCP server accepts; the in-app assistant's prompt is byte-for-byte unchanged. The contradiction was reproduced with a failing test before the fix, and the full native test binary passes after it. Nothing is committed.

## Problem

Reproduced on this worktree (same source as `198c64606f` for these files). Against unchanged source, the new wire test showed the server's discovery instructions containing `setupTitle`, while an MCP `intent_update` call with `setupTitle` on the same server came back `chat_title_unavailable`.

## Solution

- **MCP instructions**: [McpProtocol.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp) has a new `kInstructions` constant, 741 bytes, used by `discovery` and so also by the stdio helper's `initialize`. The text it serves:

  > These tools act on the project open in the running JusPrin app, which the user may be editing at the same time. Read the current state with workspace_inspect before changing it. Where a change has a dry run (settings_preview_patch, printer_setup_preview, object_divide_preview), preview first; settings_apply_patch takes the sessionId and revision its preview returned. A stale_workspace error means the project changed after your read: read and preview again before retrying. For a print request, record the requirements the user stated as intent_update fields, and your plan with plan_set, before changing the project. Check a slice with slice_report before writing its G-code with export_file. Closing a response cancels its pending work.

- **In-app prompt**: `kPrintJourneyGuidance` in [ToolRegistry.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.hpp) keeps its text; only its comment changed, to say it serves the in-app assistant only and where MCP's text lives.
- **Guide**: one paragraph added under "Tool exposure" in [mcp-tool-extension-guide.md](agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md). You did not ask for this; drop it if unwanted.

Two things to know about the wording:

- **Revision only for settings**: only `settings_apply_patch` takes a preview's sessionId and revision. `printer_setup` and `object_divide` have previews but no such arguments, so the text says "preview first" for all three and names the revision only for settings.
- **Two old sentences dropped**: "Project Undo does not reverse preset edits" repeats the `settings_apply_patch` description. "`workspace_unavailable` means open JusPrin and a project" is already in the offline error's own message, and the server also uses that code for other conditions such as a project with no plate.

No OrcaSlicer-owned file changed.

## Tests and results

- **Wire test** in [test_mcp_runtime.cpp](tests/agent/test_mcp_runtime.cpp): the `setupTitle` call is refused with `chat_title_unavailable`, the instructions do not name `setupTitle`, and a fields-only `intent_update` succeeds over MCP.
- **Catalogue test** in [test_mcp_protocol.cpp](tests/agent/test_mcp_protocol.cpp): every snake_case identifier in the instructions is an MCP-listed tool or an MCP error code, every `_preview` tool is named, and "setupTitle", "skill" and "chat" are absent. A new preview tool will fail this until the instructions name it.
- **In-app test** in [test_openai_responses_agent.cpp](tests/agent/test_openai_responses_agent.cpp): the in-app request still carries the guidance, including the setupTitle sentence.
- **Before the fix**: the two MCP tests failed with 9 failed assertions (one was my own test's missing state store, since fixed).
- **After the fix**: the whole `agent_bridge_tests` binary passes, 4724 assertions in 268 test cases.
- **Python bridge tests** (`tests/mcp`): 18 run, 1 skipped, all pass against the rebuilt `jusprin-mcp` helper.

No existing test asserted on the old text, so none needed updating.

## Remaining issues

- **Not measured with a real client**: I did not run Claude Code or Codex against the new text, so whether models follow it better is untested.
- **Shared tool descriptions still mention in-app concepts**: the `intent_update` description says "setupTitle in an in-app chat" and its MCP schema still lists `setupTitle`.
- **`settings_apply_patch` has an `intent` argument described as the setup title**: from reading the coordinator, MCP does not refuse it; I did not test that.

content.text:
**The issue**

JusPrin lets outside AI tools (like Claude Code) control the app through a connection called MCP. When such a tool connects, JusPrin sends it a short "how to use me" note. That note was copied from the instructions written for JusPrin's own built-in chat assistant, and it told the outside tool to record a "setup title". But JusPrin always rejects that request from outside tools, because the title belongs to the built-in chat. So every outside tool was told to make a call that could never succeed.

**The fix**

I wrote a separate note for outside tools that only describes things they are allowed to do: read the project first, preview changes before applying them, re-read if the project changed underneath, record the user's requirements and plan, and check a slice before exporting. The built-in assistant's instructions stay exactly as they were. I added tests that fail if the outside note ever again mentions something outside tools cannot use, confirmed they failed before the fix, and confirmed everything passes after it.

content.text:
The search found it, and your design point is right. You already told Codex to remove that `intent` argument two days ago, the removal was committed, but the commit never reached `jusprin-newui`. And yes: my fix only cleaned the connection note; the tool definitions themselves still tell outside callers about the setup title.

## What the search found

Found in Codex, so I did not search the Claude Code sessions.

- **Session:** Codex session started 2026-10-07 18:51, in worktree `~/.codex/worktrees/072c/JusPrin`.
- **Your request there:** "Remove the `intent` parameter from `settings_apply_patch`. Applying settings must not update a chat's intent or summary-card title."
- **Outcome:** committed as `d9ea3a2371` ("Remove settings intent coupling and streamline agent timeline") on branch `codex/remove-settings-patch-intent`.
- **Current state:** that commit is not in `jusprin-newui`, locally or on origin, which has moved 4 commits past where the branch forked. So the argument is still in the schema and the validator on this worktree.
- **Not discussed anywhere:** the MCP angle. No Codex message talks about an outside caller sending `intent` or `setupTitle`; the `chat_title_unavailable` refusal appears only in code edits, never in prose.

## Your design question

I agree. The setup title is used by one thing only: the in-app chat's setup card. So the instruction to set it belongs in the in-app assistant's prompt, where it already is. Today it also sits in two shared tool definitions that every outside caller reads:

- **`intent_update`:** its schema lists `setupTitle` and its description explains it, then the app refuses it from outside callers.
- **`settings_apply_patch`:** its `intent` argument says "Send it whenever the change came from something the user asked for". From reading the code (not run), an outside caller's value is accepted and silently dropped.

Does the tool ever know better than the agent? Only about facts the agent cannot see: who is calling, whether a chat exists, whether a title is already recorded. It never knows what the user actually asked for; only the agent has that. So the tool should not decide when a title is set.

## What I'd do next

1. Bring the already-decided removal (`d9ea3a2371`) onto `jusprin-newui`. It also carries unrelated timeline and avatar changes, so it needs a look rather than a blind cherry-pick.
2. Take `setupTitle` off the shared `intent_update` and give the in-app chat its own title-setting tool that outside callers never see. The project's tool guide already prescribes this shape for the two import tools. The refusal code then disappears.
3. Keep the connection-note change from this session; it is still correct either way.

Step 2 changes what the in-app assistant is told, so it needs a prompt evaluation run, not just unit tests. Do you want me to do steps 1 and 2 here, or only step 1?

entries.name: mcp__ccd_host__sync_with_base_branch
entries.description:
Bring this session's branch up to date with its base branch: the app fetches the base from `origin` and merges it into the branch checked out in this session's worktree, running git on the host, outside your sandbox, which cannot write the repository's protected paths (`.claude/hooks`, `.claude/skills`, `.mcp.json` and the like) that such a merge often touches. Use it instead of `git merge`/`git pull` whenever you need the base branch's latest commits, e.g. to resolve a pull request's merge conflicts.

`base` defaults to the base the app knows for this session (its open pull request's base, else the branch the worktree was cut from); you may name that branch or the repository's default branch, nothing else. Sandbox-protected files are brought in only from the repository's default branch; any other base merges only when it leaves those files alone, and a protected file both this branch and the base changed is left for a person (the call refuses). Nothing is pushed. Outcomes: merged (a merge commit or fast-forward; run the project's checks, then push), up to date, or conflicts: the merge is then left in progress with the conflicted files listed for you to resolve, `git add` and `git commit --no-edit` (protected files this branch only had an older upstream copy of are already taken from the base). `abort: true` abandons a merge left in progress instead. It refuses rather than touch uncommitted changes, another git operation in progress, files the repository routes through a content filter (git-lfs, git-crypt), a fork checkout whose origin is not the pull request's repository, or a session without its own worktree; merge yourself in those cases. In default mode the user approves each call on a card; in auto mode the app's classifier decides.

base.description: The base branch to merge, when the session's own isn't the one you need: its pull request's base, the branch the worktree was cut from, or the repository's default branch.

abort.description: true to abandon a merge this tool left in progress (git merge --abort) instead of merging.

_consent.description: Set by the app. Never set this yourself.

agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:367:| `intent_update` | M | Record what the user said about the print: a same-shape list of `
| `intent_update` | M | Record what the user said about the print: a same-shape list of `{field, value}` over the intent record. Use `assumed` for agent inferences; only values grounded in the user's statement become `user_confirmed`. An in-app chat may also send `setupTitle`, the user's stated purpose as the chat-owned title of the setup card, with or without fields; it applies no setting, and an MCP caller that sends it is refused (`chat_title_unavailable`) because the title belongs to a chat. | JusPrin intent store | 32 fields, 120-character title |
Default to both adapters when both can satisfy the same input contract. A deliberate filter is appropriate when context is supplied differently:

- `workspace_inspect` is exposed to both adapters so either can obtain a fresh completed slice identity after slicing, independently of the initial turn context;
- attachment-based import (`object_import`) is in-app-only, and path-based `object_import_file` is MCP-only, because a file reaches the app through the conversation in one case and through an explicit path in the other; that is two honest definitions over one workspace command, not one tool with forked behavior; and
- a future MCP diagnostics tool may be MCP-only if it exists to establish the external connection; and
- the printer panel's five own tools carry only the `Printer` exposure: neither adapter lists them, and the panel's conversation offers all of them in every mode and refuses what does not fit it (see "Tool budget and tool shape"). and what the model reads back from them is the tool's own result, not the host's workspace envelope

Document the reason beside the registry definition and test it. Exposure is not a place to fork behavior: if two adapters need different semantics, they need a better shared command or honestly separate definitions.

content.text:
`intent_update` is now off the MCP server, and my earlier connection-note rewrite is gone: you were right that most of it was not necessary. The whole change is now 15 lines added and 30 removed, uncommitted, on top of the merged `jusprin-newui` I just pulled.

## Your two questions

**Should outside agents have `intent_update` at all?** No. I checked what reads the recorded intent: only two read tools (`workspace_inspect` and `slice_report`) and the in-app chat's setup card. An outside agent already holds what its user said in its own conversation, so writing it into JusPrin does nothing for it. Outside agents can still read what the in-app chat recorded.

**Was the connection-note change necessary?** One line of it was. The old note pasted the in-app assistant's print guidance onto the end, and that guidance names `intent_update`, a tool outside agents no longer have. So the paste had to go. The rest (the rewritten note, the three new tests, the guide paragraph) was not necessary, and I reverted it.

## What changed

- **`intent_update`**: in-app only. Its description lost the sentences about MCP callers.
- **Refusal code**: the `chat_title_unavailable` check and its test are deleted, since no outside caller can reach the tool.
- **MCP connection note**: back to the original settings paragraph, without the pasted in-app guidance. It now reads: "Inspect the live workspace, search or read process settings, then preview a patch. Apply with the sessionId and revision from that preview. After stale_workspace, read and preview again. Project Undo does not reverse preset edits; use preset revert or an inverse patch. A workspace_unavailable error means you should open JusPrin and a project. Closing a response cancels pending work."
- **In-app prompt**: unchanged; only the comment on the shared constant now says it is in-app only.
- **Existing tests**: four tests that list or count the MCP tools were updated for one fewer tool.
- **Tool guide**: three small edits to match.

## Results

- Native test binary `agent_bridge_tests`: all 264 test cases pass (4673 assertions).
- Python bridge tests: 18 run, 1 skipped (Linux-only), all pass.
- The rebuilt stdio helper serves the note above and no longer lists `intent_update`.
- Not run: the full app and its shell harness, which call `intent_update` only through the in-app path that this change does not touch.

## One thing for you to decide

The outside note no longer says "record your plan with `plan_set`" or "check `slice_report` before exporting", because those sentences were part of the pasted in-app text. `plan_set` itself is still available to outside agents. The same question applies to it as to `intent_update`: do you want `plan_set` removed from MCP too?

content.text:
`plan_set` is now off the MCP server too, and I checked the history question by reading the code and by running a probe. Changes made by an outside tool are recorded in the same change log as manual edits, with the same before-and-after values, but the log cannot tell an outside tool from the built-in assistant.

## History check

**How it works.** JusPrin does not record edits per caller. The workspace watches the project itself (undo steps, setting values, preset switches) and writes one change-log entry per edit, whoever made it. While any tool call runs, the entry is stamped "agent"; otherwise "person". Outside tools and the built-in assistant run through that same code path.

**What I ran.** A throwaway test (since deleted) made one manual edit, two edits through the real MCP server, and one through the in-app path, then printed the stored log:

```
kind=setting actor=person label=Wall loops 2->3              (manual edit)
kind=setting actor=agent  label=Wall loops 3->4              (outside tool, process setting)
kind=step    actor=agent  label=Change object settings       (outside tool, undo step)
kind=setting actor=agent  label=Wall loops 4->6              (outside tool, object override)
kind=setting actor=agent  label=Wall loops 4->5              (built-in assistant)
```

The tool-call records stored beside it do say where each call came from: `source=mcp` for the outside tool, `source=agent` for the built-in assistant.

**Gaps I found:**

- **No way to tell who the "Agent" was.** An outside tool's change is stored and displayed as "Agent", identical to the built-in assistant. The page receives the `source` field on tool calls but never uses it.
- **No card for the outside call.** The page only draws a tool call under the chat message that made it. An outside call belongs to no message, so the user sees the change row but not the call.
- **It lands in whatever chat is open.** The change is attached to the active chat even though that chat did not cause it, and that chat's setup card then treats the settings as agent-made.

**Limits of this check.** The probe used the test stand-in for the workspace, not the real app. For the real app I only read the code: edit detection runs inside the tool call, and a version checkpoint is saved before and after any tool change regardless of caller. One case I did not verify: arrange or auto-orient jobs that finish after the tool call returns may be logged as "person".

## `plan_set` removal

- **Change:** same shape as `intent_update`: in-app only. Outside tools can still read the plan and intent.
- **Tests:** the native `agent_bridge_tests` binary passes all 264 test cases (4665 assertions); the Python bridge tests ran 18, 1 skipped as Linux-only, all pass.
- **Catalogue:** MCP now offers 27 tools, down from 29 at the start of the session.

Nothing is committed; the whole change is 18 lines added and 32 removed.

## Decision for you

Do you want outside-tool changes labelled as such in the history (for example "External tool" instead of "Agent")? The source is already stored on each tool call, so it is a small change: carry it onto the change entry and word the row differently. Say if you want it.

content.text:
Changes made by an outside tool are now labelled "External tool" in the history instead of "Agent". All tests pass; nothing is committed, and I have not built or run the full app, only the GUI-free test binary and the page's test suite.

## What changed

- **Recording:** each change-log entry now carries a flag saying it came through the MCP server. The tool runner already knew the caller; it now passes that along when it stamps an edit. The flag is saved with the project and survives a reload. Older saved projects have no flag and read as before.
- **Display:** a flagged row reads, for example, "Wall loops 3 → 4" with "External tool, in Strong · 10:42" underneath, where an in-app change says "Agent" and a manual one says "you".
- **Grouping:** the built-in assistant's setting changes fold into a compact "N settings" block that has no "who" label. External-tool changes are kept out of that block and shown one row per setting, like manual edits, so the label is always visible. An external run also never merges with an adjacent in-app run.

The main edits are in [Workspace.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp), [ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp) and [ChangeRows.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/ChangeRows.tsx).

## What did not change

Everything else still treats an external-tool change as an agent change. In particular the open chat's setup card still counts those settings as agent-made, and the change still lands in whichever chat is open. You asked only for the label, so I left those alone.

## Tests

- **Native** (`agent_bridge_tests`): all 265 test cases pass (4677 assertions). One new test makes a manual edit, an edit through the real MCP server and an in-app edit, reloads the saved project, and checks only the MCP one is flagged.
- **Page** (Agent UI): type-check clean; all 402 tests pass. One new test checks three external setting changes render as three rows each saying "External tool, in Strong" and not as the grouped block.
- **Python bridge tests:** not re-run after this last change, which does not touch the bridge; they passed (18 run, 1 skipped) after the `plan_set` removal.

## Not verified

- The label was checked by the page's rendering tests, not by eye in the running app. "External tool" is longer than "Agent", so the row's second line is worth a glance for wrapping in a narrow panel.
- The full app was not compiled. The shared header I changed is also used by the app's real workspace code; the change keeps the old call form valid, so I expect it to compile, but that is untested.
- Still open from before: arrange or auto-orient jobs that finish after the tool call returns may be logged as "you".
