<pasted_content id="6037">
Why would it be logged as me?
It wouldn’t. That caveat was a guess I hadn’t checked, and having now read the code, it doesn’t hold.
My worry was this: a change is labelled by who is “in the room” at the moment the history entry is written. While a tool call runs, entries are stamped Agent or External tool; the rest of the time they are stamped “you”. Arrange and auto-orient are background jobs that finish after the tool call has returned, so I assumed their result would be written to the history late, with nobody in the room, and fall back to “you”.
That is not how it works:

* The history entry is written when the undo step is taken, not when the job finishes. For arrange, the undo step “Lay out plates” is taken inside the tool call (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1213), before the job starts. Auto-orient does the same: the comment at OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1434 says the snapshot was already taken above.
* The job’s finishing step takes no undo step. I read `ArrangeJob::finalize` (ArrangeJob.cpp:610) and `OrientJob::finalize` (OrientJob.cpp:199); neither one does. The history only gains an entry for a new undo step, an undo or redo, a setting change, or a preset switch, so the job ending writes nothing.

So an arrange or auto-orient started by a tool gets one entry, correctly labelled Agent or External tool, and nothing is added later under your name.
One limit on this: I read the two finishing functions themselves, not every function they call (for example the plate-rebuilding code arrange runs at the end). I saw no sign that those take an undo step, but I did not trace them, and none of this was run in the real app.
</pasted_content id="6037">

 Does it mean that we're all in the clear?  If so, commit.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Stop offering intent_update and plan_set to MCP clients

The MCP server's connection instructions ended with the in-app assistant's
print guidance, which told every external client to record a setup title
with intent_update. The server always refused that call from MCP
(chat_title_unavailable), because the title belongs to an in-app chat.

The intent record and the pinned plan serve the in-app chat only: its setup
card, and what its user told it. An external agent keeps what its user said,
and its plan, in its own conversation. So:

- intent_update and plan_set are in-app only. MCP clients can still read
  the intent and the plan through workspace_inspect and slice_report.
- The MCP instructions no longer carry the in-app print guidance, which
  names those two tools. The in-app assistant's prompt is unchanged.
- The chat_title_unavailable refusal and its test are removed: no MCP
  caller can reach intent_update any more.

The MCP catalogue goes from 29 tools to 27.
EOF
git add -A agent-docs src tests && git diff --cached --stat | tail -1 && git diff --cached --check && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Label edits made by an external tool in the change log

An edit made through the MCP server was recorded in the change log as the
in-app Agent's, so the thread showed "Agent" for a change that an external
client such as Claude Code made.

The tool coordinator now tells the workspace which caller a command came
from, and a change entry an external tool caused is saved with
"external": true. Its actor stays "agent", so everything that treats agent
edits alike (undo of an agent step, the setup card) behaves as before, and
projects saved earlier load unchanged.

In the thread an external tool's edits read "External tool" where an in-app
change reads "Agent". They are drawn one row per edit, like hand edits, and
are kept out of the in-app Agent's grouped settings block, which has no
room to say who made a change.
EOF
git log --oneline -3 && git status --short | head

Yes on the "logged as you" worry, and I've committed. Two commits are on this worktree's branch (`claude/interesting-hodgkin-61f1a8`), not pushed and not yet on `jusprin-newui`.

## Is the side chat right?

I checked its claims against the code myself and they hold:

- **The history entry is written inside the tool call.** For arrange, the undo step "Lay out plates" is taken before the job starts; auto-orient takes its step earlier in the same call too.
- **The jobs add nothing when they finish.** Neither the arrange job's source file nor the auto-orient job's contains any undo step at all.
- **The part the side chat did not trace is also clean.** I followed the arrange job's finishing code into the plate-rebuilding and object-list-reloading functions it calls. The plate code has exactly one undo step, in the function that switches the selected plate, and I found no call to it on that path.

So a tool-started arrange or auto-orient gets one entry, labelled Agent or External tool, and nothing later under your name. This is from reading the code, not from running the real app.

## What is still unverified

- **Not seen by eye.** The "External tool" row was checked by the page's rendering tests only. It is longer than "Agent", so it may wrap in a narrow panel.
- **Full app not built.** I syntax-checked the app's real workspace source against my shared-header change and it is clean, but I did not build or launch the app.

Neither blocked the commit for me: both changes are covered by passing tests (265 native test cases, 402 page tests, 18 Python bridge tests with one Linux-only skip).

## Commits

- `6277ae02fa` Stop offering intent_update and plan_set to MCP clients
- `98c2e8b784` Label edits made by an external tool in the change log
